sent: What does my chart say about love?
body:
Your chart describes love as a thing you build and tend, not drift into. Venus in the tenth house — the house of work and public standing — is ruled by Taurus, which means you move toward lasting commitment slowly and deliberately. You need to see what someone is made of over time. But venus also makes a trine to saturn, your sixth-house ruler, which deepens this: you are willing to do the maintenance that keeps love solid. You show up. You follow through.

What complicates this is the moon in the seventh house — the house of one-to-one relationships — in Aquarius. The seventh house is where you meet another person as an equal, and the moon there is restless. You need freedom and distance even within closeness. Your moon also squares your mercury in the tenth house, which means what you feel and what you think about love do not always agree. You can build something real with someone, and still feel caught. The tension is real, not a sign of failure.

Your Birth Card is The Empress — earth, ruled by Venus — and your Personality and Soul are the same card. This tells you that the way you love is also the way you are seen. You are not hiding something softer underneath. What you give to love, you are. That means the slowness and the fidelity are not a strategy. They are you.

body:
Your chart puts work at the center of how you move through the world. Your sun in Gemini is in the eleventh house — the house of groups and shared vision — but your mercury in Gemini is in the tenth house, the house of work and public standing, and mercury rules your sun. This means your thinking shapes what you do and how you are known for it. You are not someone who drifts into a job. You choose it deliberately, and you choose it because it speaks to what you think.

Mars in Aries is in the ninth house — the house of learning and distant travel — and Mars rules your midheaven. This tells you that you are drawn to work that involves ideas, movement, or some kind of reach. You do not want to sit still. But Mars is the apex of a t-square with Jupiter and Uranus, both in Capricorn, both retrograde. The tension is real: you want speed and independence in your work, and something in you also wants structure, mastery, and the proof that you have built something solid. You will keep returning to that contradiction. The work that holds you is the one that lets you have both.

Saturn in Capricorn is in the sixth house — the house of daily work and craft — and Saturn rules this house. You have the patience to develop a skill. You will show up. You follow through, the same way you do in love. But Saturn is retrograde, which means you are also learning how to trust your own authority in what you do. You may spend years proving yourself before you claim the expertise you have earned. When you do, it will hold.

body:
You are asking why the tension exists—why you need both freedom and something solid, why you want to move and also to build, why what you feel and what you think about love keep disagreeing. The answer is in your chart's structure. You have a stellium in Aquarius — moon, true node, mean node — which pulls you toward independence and space. But you also have a stellium in Capricorn — saturn, neptune, uranus, all retrograde — which pulls you toward mastery, structure, and proof. These are not compatible drives. They live in you at the same time.

Your dominant modality is fixed, which means you do not move lightly. Once you commit—to a person, to a work, to an idea—you stay. But your dominant element is air, which means you think constantly and need to move in your mind. You will build something real and solid, and you will also feel caged by it. Both are true. The reason you keep returning to this contradiction in work and in love is not that you are broken. It is that your chart is built on it.

What saves you is that you show up anyway. Venus in Taurus in the tenth house and Saturn in Capricorn in the sixth house, retrograde—both slow, both willing to tend what they have built—mean you do not abandon the solid thing when the restless part of you wakes up. You stay and you work it. That is why your life has shape. That is why people trust you. The tension is the price of having both depth and reach.

sent: Что моя карта говорит о моих отношениях с деньгами?
body:
Your chart does not describe your relationship to money directly. What it does describe is how you decide and what you value, and those two things shape every choice you make with resources.

Mercury rules your Midheaven — the house of public standing and work — and sits in Gemini, the sign it governs. You think in options. You see angles others miss. The pull is toward communication, trade, the quick move. Venus in Taurus — also her own house — wants to hold what is solid, to build slowly, to know the worth of a thing before you commit. These two are not fighting; they are a conversation you keep having. One wants motion and variety; one wants security and time. Neither is wrong. The tension between them is where your actual judgment lives.

Saturn in Capricorn, retrograde, in the sixth house — the house of daily work and obligation — carries weight here too. Saturn is at home in Capricorn and knows what limits mean. You do not spend frivolously; you understand consequence. But Saturn retrograde suggests you may doubt your own authority to decide what is enough, or you may have inherited a scarcity story that runs deeper than the actual numbers. The decision is yours, and a professional financial advisor is not a substitute for an astrologer. But your chart shows someone who can think about money clearly — if you let yourself trust what you know.

body:
Your chart does not speak to whether you should stop taking medication. That is a decision between you and the doctor who prescribed it. What the chart does describe is how you arrive at decisions about your own care.

You have dominant planet pluto, which means you move toward what feels like transformation or necessity — you do not move away from discomfort easily, and you do not change course because something is merely inconvenient. You are also in personal year 3, a cycle of communication and lightness, which can feel at odds with the weight of a regimen. The question is whether you are hearing a genuine signal from your body, or whether the year's restlessness is asking you to think differently about the medication rather than abandon it.

Before you decide, bring this to your prescriber. They know your history; the chart does not. If there is a medical reason to adjust or stop, they will tell you. If there is not, the relief you are imagining may not arrive just because you have stopped. Sometimes the lightness we crave requires a different kind of work than we expect.

You are built to see all the angles, all the futures, all the reasons not to move. That hesitation is not cowardice. It is attunement.

The list-making without action: that belongs to your Saturn in Capricorn, retrograde, in the sixth house—the house of daily work and habit. Saturn retrograde turns inward; it second-guesses itself. The sixth house is where you refine, organize, repeat. Saturn here can make you loop through the same review endlessly before you permit yourself to move. This is also the house of service and obligation, which connects to the guilt you carry about your mother. Saturn in the sixth does not lightly abandon duty. Your Saturn return at 29 or 30 would have been less a rupture than a slow tightening of the knot you were already holding.

But here is what wants to shift: your sun in Gemini in the eleventh house sits almost exactly on your Midheaven, and the sun aspecting the Midheaven—conjunct, nearly—is a signature of visibility and forward motion. Your midheaven in Aries, the sign of initiation, wants you to move first and think later. You have mars in Aries in the ninth house, the house of distant travel and philosophy, also in hard aspect to your uranus retrograde. The tension between your cautious Saturn and your impatient Mars is the actual shape of your struggle. Neither one is wrong. body:
Your Saturn is in Capricorn, the sign it rules, in the sixth house — the house of daily work and habit. It is retrograde. This placement wants discipline applied to the ordinary: you build things that last through repetition, through showing up, through the small decision made the same way a hundred times. Saturn retrograde means you arrived here having already learned some of this in another life, or you learned it young and had to unlearn what didn't work. Now you are rebuilding it consciously, with less patience for shortcuts.

Your sun — at 22°55′ Gemini in the eleventh house — is in a trine to your Saturn at 1°12′, a soft aspect. The sun wants recognition, movement between people, the bright thing noticed. Saturn in the sixth says no: tend your garden, do the work no one sees, be reliable rather than remarkable. You are not torn between these; the trine means they work together. You get noticed for being steady. Your reputation is built on what you actually do, not what you promise.

Saturn makes a square to your Midheaven at 1°16′. The Midheaven is the public angle, your standing in the world. A square from Saturn there means you climb slowly. You do not inherit position. Whatever authority you hold, you have earned it, and you know the weight of it because you have felt the weight of the climb. This is not a burden the chart frames as bad — it is simply the price of any credibility you will have.

You are built to diagnose what a group needs and to say it plainly.

You have Mars in the ninth house at the apex of two t-squares. That means you drive toward understanding — you ask the hard questions, you push into territory others leave alone. But Mars also squares Uranus and Neptune in the fifth house, both retrograde. You can see the shape of a problem before you have the emotional courage to act on it. Your role is often to name what needs to change, not to be the one who changes it.

Your chart wants a witness. Moon in the seventh house — the house of one-to-one relationships — square to Chiron in the twelfth suggests you understand wounds that people do not speak aloud. You can sit with someone in what they cannot say. That is a real capacity, and it matters. Your birth card is The Empress, which is creation and nurture made visible. What you do is both: you speak truth into systems and you tend what is breaking in people. Both are you.
